[=Wiki Syntax=]

This page describes the current wiki behavior implemented by [.txt|js/viewer.wiki.js.] and [.txt|index.html.].
Those files are the authority when this quick sheet and older examples disagree.

[=Basic Principle=]

Most syntax uses bracketed forms.
Block syntax on its own line creates its own element.
Inline syntax only affects running text.

Lines without a block marker and with the same indentation join into one paragraph.
Line breaks inside such a paragraph render like soft wraps.
An empty line ends the paragraph.

That means:

- a single source line break inside a paragraph is rendered as a space
- use an empty line if you want a visible paragraph break

Where it stays readable, this page shows examples as [.txt|Source.] versus [.txt|Rendered.] in tables so the syntax and the live result stay together.

[=Escapes=]
[| [*Source*]  | [*Rendered*] |]
[| [.txt|[[.]  | [[           |]
[| [.txt|]].]  | ]]           |]
[| [.txt|[|].] | [|]          |]

[=Headings=]

There is exactly one heading form:

[.txt
|[=Title=]
.]

- headings start at the beginning of the line
- headings appear in the table of contents
- there is no second or third heading level; [.txt|[==Title==].] and [.txt|[===Title===].] are invalid

[=Lists=]

The block list markers are:

[| [*Source*] | [*Rendered*] |]
[|
  [.txt
  |- Dash marker
  |o Circle marker
  |* Dot marker
  |# Square marker
  |> Arrow marker
  .]
|
  - Dash marker
  o Circle marker
  * Dot marker
  # Square marker
  > Arrow marker
|]

- each marked line becomes its own list item
- multi-line list items are currently not joined automatically

[=Inline Formatting=]
[| [*Feature*]    | [*Source*]             | [*Rendered*]  |]
[| underlined     | [.txt| XXX[_YYY_]ZZZ.] | XXX[_YYY_]ZZZ |]
[| struck through | [.txt| XXX[-YYY-]ZZZ.] | XXX[-YYY-]ZZZ |]
[| italic         | [.txt| XXX[/YYY/]ZZZ.] | XXX[/YYY/]ZZZ |]
[| bold           | [.txt| XXX[*YYY*]ZZZ.] | XXX[*YYY*]ZZZ |]
[| red            | [.txt| XXX[!YYY!]ZZZ.] | XXX[!YYY!]ZZZ |]
[| smaller Text   | [.txt| XXX[(YYY)]ZZZ.] | XXX[(YYY)]ZZZ |]
[| superscript    | [.txt| XXX['YYY']ZZZ.] | XXX['YYY']ZZZ |]
[| subscript      | [.txt| XXX[,YYY,]ZZZ.] | XXX[,YYY,]ZZZ |]

- inline markers may be nested if they close correctly

[=Links=]

Normal wiki links use the less-than form:

[| [*Source*]                                    | [*Rendered*]                          |]
[| [.txt|[<../TODO.wiki|TODO File>].]            | [<../TODO.wiki|TODO File>]            |]
[| [.txt|[<https://example.com|External Link>].] | [<https://example.com|External Link>] |]

Important rules:

- a target without an extension is treated as a wiki page and gets [.txt|.wiki.] implicitly
- [.txt|.wiki.], [.txt|.spo.], [.txt|.ilt.], [.txt|.mermaid.], and [.txt|.mmd.] open in repo viewers
- explicit targets with other extensions resolve as files or assets
- raw URLs, [.txt|www.example.com.], and mail addresses are auto-linked
- the legacy board-link form [.txt|[?Title?].] is still recognized

[=Paragraphs Tables and Rules=]

Paragraph indentation is preserved by shared leading spaces/tabs.
Two consecutive text lines are merged into one paragraph.
If you want a new paragraph, you must insert an empty line in the source.

Visible rule:

[| [*Source*]    | [*Rendered*] |]
[| [.txt|[---].] | [---]        |]

Tables use consecutive lines that begin with [.txt|[|.]:

[.txt
|[| [*Name*] | [*Value*] |]
|[| Alpha    | 1         |]
|[| A [|] B  | 2         |]
.]

- table cell separators ignore nested wiki syntax
- use [.txt|[|].] for a literal pipe inside a cell

[| [*Source*] | [*Rendered*] |]
[|
  [.txt
  |This is a paragraph.
  |This line still belongs to it.
  .]
|
  This is a paragraph.
  This line still belongs to it.
|]
[|
  [.txt
  |First paragraph.
  |
  |Second paragraph.
  .]
|
  First paragraph.
  
  Second paragraph.
|]
[|
  [.txt
  |  This paragraph is indented.
  |  This line as well.
  .]
|
  This paragraph is indented.
  This line as well.
|]
[|
  [.txt
  |[---]
  .]
|
  [---]
|]
[|
  [.txt
  |[| [*Name*] | [*Value*] |]
  |[| Alpha    | 1         |]
  |[| A [|] B  | 2         |]
  .]
|
  [| [*Name*] | [*Value*] |]
  [| Alpha    | 1         |]
  [| A [|] B  | 2         |]
|]

[=External Resource Blocks=]

Hash blocks reference files or URLs:

[| [*Source*] | [*Rendered*] |]
[|
  [.txt
  |[# ../SPO_CS/Regression.Tests/01_03_AssignInt.SPO #]
  .]
|
  [# ../SPO_CS/Regression.Tests/01_03_AssignInt.SPO #]
|]

- paths are relative to the current wiki file
- [.txt|.wiki.], [.txt|.spo.], [.txt|.ilt.], [.txt|.mermaid.], and [.txt|.mmd.] use viewers
- images and videos use built-in media rendering
- plain text files without a dedicated viewer fall back to code-style rendering

[=Embedded Resource Blocks=]

Embedded resources use a standalone opener line and the matching standalone close line shown below:

[| [*Source*] | [*Rendered*] |]
[|
  [.txt
  |[.txt
  ||first line
  ||second line
  |.]
  .]
|
  [.txt
  |first line
  |second line
  .]
|]
[|
  [.txt
  |[.spo
  ||x := 1
  ||export x
  |.]
  .]
|
  [.spo
  |x := 1
  |export x
  .]
|]

- for text resources, a leading helper pipe character on each content line is stripped
- binary resources use Base64 between the opener and the matching close line

[=Inline Compact Objects=]

Inside a paragraph, compact forms stay inline:

[| [*Source*] | [*Rendered*] |]
[|
  [.txt
  |Text with [# ../SPO_CS/Regression.Tests/01_03_AssignInt.SPO #] in a sentence.
  .]
|
  Text with [# ../SPO_CS/Regression.Tests/01_03_AssignInt.SPO #] in a sentence.
|]
[|
  [.txt
  |Text with [.spo|x := 1.] in a sentence.
  .]
|
  Text with [.spo|§DEF x := 1.] in a sentence.
|]

- inline hash objects render as compact references or previews
- inline dot objects render as compact code/resource chips
- if you want the large block renderer, use the standalone block form instead

[=Binary vs Text=]

The embedded-resource switch is file-extension based.

The following extensions are currently treated as binary:

- [.txt|avif.], [.txt|bmp.], [.txt|gif.], [.txt|ico.], [.txt|jpeg.], [.txt|jpg.]
- [.txt|mp3.], [.txt|mp4.], [.txt|ogv.], [.txt|pdf.], [.txt|png.]
- [.txt|wav.], [.txt|webm.], [.txt|webp.], [.txt|zip.]

Everything else is currently treated as text.

[=Viewers By Extension=]

There are dedicated viewers for:

- [.txt|wiki.]
- [.txt|spo.] and [.txt|ilt.]
- [.txt|mermaid.] and [.txt|mmd.]

There are built-in media fallbacks for:

- images such as [.txt|avif.], [.txt|bmp.], [.txt|gif.], [.txt|ico.], [.txt|jpeg.], [.txt|jpg.], [.txt|png.], [.txt|svg.], [.txt|webp.]
- videos such as [.txt|mp4.], [.txt|ogv.], [.txt|webm.]

[=Practical Notes=]

- use a standalone [.txt|.txt.] block for raw syntax examples
- escape literal brackets and pipe characters inside running text
- keep headings flat; use inline emphasis instead of fake heading levels
- relative paths may use [.txt|..], but they still stay inside the allowed viewer root
